page: Amazon Web Services m8id.48xlarge is a general-purpose, Nitro-virtualized instance equipped with dedicated Intel Xeon 6975P-C processors. The system delivers 96 physical cores and 192 virtual CPUs running at 3.9 GHz, backed by 480 MB of shared L3 cache and support for Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 vector instructions. Memory provisioning includes 768.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, maintaining a balanced 4:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Complementing the compute architecture is an integrated 11,400 GB NVMe SSD instance storage volume and a 75 Gbps baseline network interface, operating without attached discrete GPUs.

Benchmark results place the m8id.48xlarge in the top tier across parallelized compute, in-memory operations, and I/O tasks. It exhibits top-tier multi-threaded decompression throughput of 1,306.18 GB/sec in bzip3, a PassMark CPU score of 143,956.66, and elevated performance in software compilation and cryptographic workloads. Memory throughput is equally robust, reaching 587.33 GB/sec in large uncached reads and 242.09 GB/sec in writes. For transactional and key-value workloads, the server achieved top-tier marks with 247.82 million Redis SET operations per second and high-throughput static web serving at 264.3 GB/sec. LLM prompt ingestion also demonstrates strong multi-core scaling, reaching 4,230.34 tokens/sec on lightweight models.

The primary operational tradeoff relates to per-core versus multi-core performance density. While stress-ng single-core performance registers in the average bracket, the massive 192-thread capacity and top-tier multi-core marks make it cost-efficient for heavy concurrency and multi-tenant consolidation rather than strictly single-threaded tasks. The substantial direct-attached 11.4 TB NVMe array delivers massive local IOPS without relying solely on remote network-attached volumes, lowering storage latency overhead.

Given its hardware scale and high memory bandwidth, the m8id.48xlarge is optimal for high-throughput distributed databases, enterprise in-memory caches, large-scale CI/CD build environments, batch ETL pipelines, and CPU-driven machine learning inference tasks.
description: Amazon Web Services m8id.48xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 192 vCPUs across 96 physical cores powered by Intel Xeon 6975P-C processors at 3.9 GHz. Built on the AWS Nitro System, it couples 768.0 GB of DDR5 system memory with 11,400 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage and 75 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Synthetic benchmarks indicate top-tier multi-threaded computational power, memory bandwidth, and caching speed, with Redis processing achieving 247.82 million operations per second and strong multi-core software compilation scores. Single-core throughput is moderate by comparison, positioning the platform for highly parallel workloads rather than single-threaded bottlenecks. Its dense resource allocation and integrated high-capacity NVMe drive make it well matched for distributed database clusters, enterprise caching systems, heavy CI/CD pipelines, big data analytics, and CPU-based deep learning inference.
